attacks.attack_command: PricingService::calculateOrder() called with PricingRequest containing items {item_id, quantity, total: 0.01, price: 0.01}; DB item price = 7.00
attacks.rationale: HTTP+auth orchestration unnecessary — SSOT property lives in service layer, not controller. Tested at service layer directly per advisor guidance.
attacks.defense_response: PricingRequest is a `final readonly` class (app/Services/Pricing/PricingRequest.php:10) with NO `total` field. Only `requestItems` array, branchId, orderId, couponId, customerUserId, deliveryCharge etc. are accepted. Inside calculateOrder() (PricingService.php:36-309), server re-queries `Item::query()->select('id','price','tax_id')->whereIn('id', $requestedItemIds)` and builds composition_snapshot+totals exclusively from DB rows (`$dbItem->price`). Client `total`/`price` fields are not read.
attacks.empirical_result: CLIENT_CLAIMED=0.01 → SERVER_COMPUTED_SUBTOTAL=7 → SERVER_TOTAL=7 (DB item.price=7.00). Client tampering ignored at SSOT layer.
